lemma: RANK-CELL LEMMA (not a closure of G0001). Let W be a k x f integer matrix of free-variable weights of k non-constant surviving THR gates on {0,1}^f, with real rank r. Then the number of distinct joint output patterns (indicators [W_j . x >= t_j]) over x in {0,1}^f is at most sum_{i<=r} C(k,i). Proof: (1) factor W = P Q with Q an r x f real matrix; each gate value depends on x only through y = Qx in R^r. (2) Let delta > 0 be below every nonzero |P_j . Qx - t_j| over the finite cube; then [P_j . y >= t_j] = [P_j . y - (t_j - delta) > 0] on the cube, so each joint pattern is realised by a point of the arrangement of the k affine hyperplanes {P_j . y = t_j - delta} in R^r, and distinct patterns lie in distinct open cells. (3) k affine hyperplanes in R^r have at most sum_{i<=r} C(k,i) open cells (induction R(k,r) <= R(k-1,r) + R(k-1,r-1)). Hence patterns <= sum_{i<=r} C(k,i). Known as the Cover/Zaslavsky cell count; the contribution here is only its application to the restricted gate family.

proved_step: PROOF. Put lo = sum_{i in F} min(w_i,0), hi = sum_{i in F} max(w_i,0). Restricted g is constant 1 iff V+lo >= t, constant 0 iff V+hi < t, where V = sum_{i not in F} w_i b_i. So g is non-constant iff V lies in [t-hi, t-lo), a set of hi-lo = W_F consecutive integers. Erdos (1945) Littlewood-Offord: for integers |c_i|>=1, any open interval of length 2 contains at most C(N,floor(N/2)) of the 2^N sums of subsets of {c_i}. Apply it to 2V - sum w_i = sum w_i eps_i with eps_i = 2b_i - 1 (nonzero coefficients only; zero weights contribute constants) to get max_x Pr[V=x] <= C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N. Union over the W_F integer values gives the first inequality; C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N <= 1/sqrt(N) gives the second. For N=0 the bound is W_F and is trivially valid. CORROLLARY: E_F[W_F] = (k/n) sum_i |w_i| <= kKs/n. Since N >= s-k deterministically: if s >= 2k, 1/sqrt(s-k) <= sqrt(2/s), so the bound is <= sqrt(2) kK sqrt(s)/n <= sqrt(2) kK/sqrt(n). If s < 2k, use the bound with c <= 1: kKs/n <= 2k^2K/n <= sqrt(2) kK/sqrt(n) since k^2 <= n/2. Summing over gates gives the stated count.

Setup: w_1..w_m in Z^n, thresholds t_1..t_m, a set F of k free coordinates, complement R with |R| = n-k, and a fixed assignment b in {0,1}^R. Restricted gate g_j|_b(y) = [sum_{i in F} w_ji y_i >= t_j - S_j(b)], S_j(b) = sum_{q in R} w_jq b_q, for y in {0,1}^F. Claim: the number of distinct functions {0,1}^F -> {0,1} among {g_j|_b : j <= m} is at most sum_{i=0}^{k+1} C(2^k, i) <= (2^k+1)^{k+1} <= 2^{(k+1)^2}, independent of m and n. Sauer-Shelah applied to the family of traces on the 2^k-point cube gives at most sum_{i<=k+1} C(2^k,i) distinct traces. Distinct functions are distinct traces, so the bound follows. QED. Exact finite check cm-36040ff49f6d41f0 (k <= 3) gives threshold counts 4, 14, 104 matching the known counts, with 0 violations. At k of order sqrt(n) (the regime of G0001), D_k is about 2^n, which exceeds m. It does not bound the surviving count itself and does not give a joint description of the m gates across all restrictions b.

lemma: SURVIVOR COMPRESSION (bounded weights, R0837). Let w_1..w_m in Z^n with |w_{j,i}| <= K, thresholds T_j, a k-set F, and a fixing b in {0,1}^{[n]\F}. PROOF: for fixed u in [-K,K]^F the values u.x (x in {0,1}^F) lie in an integer interval of length 2Kk, so at most 2Kk+1 distinct values; a non-constant table x -> [u.x >= tau] is determined by the cut among the distinct values, so at most 2Kk non-constant tables per u; the restricted weight vectors lie in [-K,K]^F, so at most (2K+1)^k choices of u; union bound. Consequence: the restricted top sum equals const + sum over at most D_k fixed tables of coefficient * table (exact identity).

proved_step: LEMMA (bounded-weight table count, complete proof). Let K, k >= 1, let U = [-K,K]^k, and let T_{K,k} be the set of NON-CONSTANT functions {0,1}^k -> {0,1} of the form x -> [u.x >= tau] with u in U and tau in Z. Then |T_{K,k}| <= 2Kk(2K+1)^k. The table x -> [u.x >= tau] is constant unless lo < tau <= hi, and for tau in (lo,hi] the table is determined by tau, giving at most hi - lo <= 2Kk distinct non-constant tables per u. There are (2K+1)^k vectors u, so the union bound gives the claim. Consequence (exact identity): for any surviving bottom gates with weights in U and any top weights v, the restricted top sum equals a constant plus sum over T in T_{K,k} of c_T * T, with c_T the sum of v_j over gates whose restricted table is T.

proved_step: LEMMA (K = 1 repair of the SURVIVOR COMPRESSION step; does NOT close G0001). Statement: let n, k >= 1, F subset [n], |F| = k, weights w_j in {-1,0,1}^n for j = 1..m, integer thresholds T_j, and a fixing b in {0,1}^([n] minus F). Define g_{j,b}(x) = [sum_{i in F} w_{j,i} x_i >= T_j - sum_{i not in F} w_{j,i} b_i] for x in {0,1}^F. Then the number of distinct functions {0,1}^F -> {0,1} among all g_{j,b} (over all j and b) is at most 3^k (2k+2). PROOF: fix j, b. Put v = (w_{j,i})_{i in F} in {-1,0,1}^F and tau = T_j - sum_{i notin F} w_{j,i} b_i in Z. Then g_{j,b}(x) = [s(x) >= tau] with s(x) = v.x, and s(x) is an integer in [-k, k] for all x in {0,1}^F. Replace tau by tau' = min(max(tau, -k), k+1). If tau < -k then tau' = -k and both functions are identically 1, since s(x) >= -k. If tau > k+1 then tau' = k+1 and both functions are identically 0, since s(x) <= k. Otherwise tau' = tau. So g_{j,b} = [v.x >= tau'] with tau' in {-k, ..., k+1}, a set of 2k+2 values. Hence each restricted function is determined by the pair (v, tau') in {-1,0,1}^F x {-k..k+1}, which has 3^k (2k+2) elements. Counting these pairs bounds the number of distinct functions. Non-constant ones form a subset. QED. SCOPE: holds for all n, k, m with weights in {-1,0,1}. It is non-trivial only when 3^k(2k+2) < m, i.e. k below about log_3 m (about 0.95 log_2 n for m = n^1.5). At k = floor((1/2) log_3 n) the count is at most sqrt(n)(2 log_3 n + 2), which is below the number of surviving gates n log n in the window lemma regime. WHY THIS DOES NOT CLOSE G0001: G0001 asks for a bound on sum_l K_l (the total OBDD size over all levels for a constructible order), and this lemma bounds only the distinct restricted functions for ONE fixed set F of k variables, for a restricted range of k. It does not bound the number of distinct residual functions at all levels with 2^(n-k) assignments. Also, the lemma gives no saving at k ~ sqrt(n), where the refuted bound applies. lemma: VC COUNT OF RESTRICTED BOTTOM GATES (no weight bound). Let k >= 1, N = 2^k, and let H_k = { x -> [u.x >= tau] restricted to {0,1}^k : u in R^k, tau in R }. Then |H_k| <= sum_{i=0}^{k+1} C(2^k, i) <= (k+2) * 2^{k(k+1)}. Consequently, for any family of m bottom THR gates on n variables and any k-set F of free variables and any fixing b of the other variables, the number of distinct NON-CONSTANT restricted tables is at most min(m, (k+2) 2^{k(k+1)}), independent of the weight bound K and of the thresholds. PROOF. (1) Lift x -> (x,1) in R^{k+1}; then [u.x >= tau] = [(u,-tau).(x,1) >= 0], so H_k restricted to the cube is a homogeneous halfspace class in R^{k+1}, which has VC dimension k+1 (standard, Vapnik; Shalev-Shwartz and Ben-David Thm 9.2). (2) Sauer-Shelah: a class of VC dimension d on N points realises at most sum_{i<=d} C(N,i) dichotomies. Here N = 2^k points and d = k+1. (3) For i <= k+1 and N >= 1, C(N,i) <= N^i <= N^{k+1}, so the sum has at most k+2 terms each <= 2^{k(k+1)}. (4) The restricted gate g_{j,b}(x) = [sum_{i in F} w_{j,i} x_i >= T_j - sum_{i notin F} w_{j,i} b_i] is an element of H_k with u = restricted weights and tau = restricted threshold, so the distinct non-constant tables are a subset of H_k. QED. SCOPE AND LIMITS (checked by hand): for k = 2, H_2 has 14 non-constant threshold tables, consistent with the bound 4 * 2^6 = 256. The bound beats the earlier D_k = 2Kk(2K+1)^k only when K is large relative to 2^k (roughly K >= 2^k); for K = 1 it is weaker.

By Sauer-Shelah lemma, the number of distinct traces on a set of size 2^k is at most sum_{i=0}^{k+1} C(2^k, i). This bound is independent of m and n.
